repository.name: vllm-project/vllm
repository.language: Python (plus CUDA/C++ in csrc/, Rust in rust/)

project_overview.what_it_is: vLLM is a high-throughput, low-latency inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models. It provides an offline LLM API, an OpenAI-compatible HTTP/gRPC server, and a pluggable platform abstraction that supports NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel XPU, Google TPU, CPU, and out-of-tree accelerators such as Huawei Ascend (via the vllm-ascend plugin).
problems_solved: Serving many concurrent requests efficiently by sharing KV cache memory through PagedAttention and a block manager.
Scaling across tensor/pipeline/data/expert parallelism and multiple nodes via a distributed execution layer.
Reducing per-step latency with torch.compile / Inductor graph capture and CUDA graph replay (piecewise + full).
Enabling acceleration on heterogeneous hardware through a single Platform abstraction plus runtime entry-point plugins.
Accelerating generation via speculative decoding (Eagle/Eagle3/MTP/ngram/draft model), structured outputs, LoRA, quantization, and KV cache offloading/transfer.
project_overview.analysis_anchor: This knowledge snapshot is anchored at commit 73859fec58. All line references and class layouts reflect that revision. Note: the V1 monolith runner and the newer V2 runner both exist side by side (selected by vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner).

core_modules.responsibility: Hardware abstraction layer. Defines the Platform base class, built-in platform implementations (cuda/rocm/xpu/cpu/tpu/zen_cpu), and the lazy auto-detection/plugin loading of the current platform.
core_modules.implementation_principle: resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname() enumerates builtin plugins first (tpu, cuda, rocm, xpu, cpu) then OOT entry points from group 'vllm.platform_plugins'. Exactly one OOT plugin or one builtin may activate (>=2 raises). The module-level __getattr__ lazily materializes the singleton 'current_platform' by resolving the chosen qualname. Platform exposes classmethods used throughout the engine: get_attn_backend_cls, check_and_update_config, get_device_capability, get_compile_backend, get_pass_manager_cls, get_static_graph_wrapper_cls, get_device_communicator_cls, register_custom_kv_cache_specs, etc.

core_modules.responsibility: V1 engine core loop and frontend. EngineCore schedules/executes a step; EngineCoreClient transports requests/outputs (in-process or ZMQ multiprocess); LLMEngine/OutputProcessor/InputProcessor/Detokenizer form the frontend.
core_modules.implementation_principle: EngineCore.step() calls scheduler.schedule() -> executor.execute_model(non_block=True) -> future.result() (or executor.sample_tokens if model returned None) -> scheduler.update_from_output() -> EngineCoreOutputs. EngineCoreProc runs the busy loop over ZMQ sockets in a background process; InprocClient runs it inline for offline LLM. DPEngineCoreProc adds data-parallel wave balancing and elastic EP.

core_modules.responsibility: Scheduler: decides which requests run each step and how many tokens, interacts with the KV cache manager, KV/EC connectors, encoder cache, and structured outputs.
core_modules.implementation_principle: Scheduler.schedule() first schedules running requests (chunked prefill/decode, spec tokens, encoder inputs) then waiting requests if no preemption occurred. KV allocation goes through KVCacheManager.allocate_slots(); on failure it preempts a victim. update_from_output() applies sampled tokens, spec-decode acceptance, stop checks, connector outputs, and produces per-client EngineCoreOutputs. AsyncScheduler/DiffusionAsyncScheduler override _update_after_schedule/_update_request_with_output.

core_modules.responsibility: KV cache runtime: block pool, per-spec managers, coordinator with prefix caching, and the manager facade used by the scheduler.
core_modules.implementation_principle: BlockPool owns a list of KVCacheBlock objects, a free-block queue and a hash->block map for prefix caching. KVCacheCoordinator (Unitary for one group, Hybrid for many) dispatches to SingleTypeKVCacheManager subclasses (FullAttentionManager, SlidingWindowManager, MambaManager, etc). KVCacheManager is the scheduler-facing facade. Block IDs flow into SchedulerOutput and are mapped to kernel block IDs by the worker BlockTable.

core_modules.responsibility: Worker and ModelRunner: owns the model, KV cache tensors, input batch, attention metadata builders, CUDA graph dispatch, sampling, speculative drafting, and MM encoder execution.
core_modules.implementation_principle: WorkerBase defines the abstract worker contract; Worker (GPU) constructs GPUModelRunner in init_device, allocates KV cache in initialize_from_config, and delegates execute_model/sample_tokens. GPUModelRunner V1 is a monolith; GPUModelRunner V2 is decomposed into InputBuffers/BlockTables/ModelState/CUDAGraphManager/Speculator. execute_model returns None and defers sampling to sample_tokens when structured-output/parallel sampling needs it, carrying state in ExecuteModelState.

core_modules.responsibility: Attention backend framework, backend registry, runtime selector, and all concrete attention implementations (FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, MLA variants, Mamba/linear/SWA/Sink).
core_modules.implementation_principle: AttentionBackend declares static capabilities (get_name/get_impl_cls/get_builder_cls, supports_*/get_supported_kernel_block_sizes/customize_spec/validate_configuration). Platform.get_attn_backend_cls() resolves a class path, selector.get_attn_backend() assembles AttentionSelectorConfig and memoizes via functools.cache. Per-layer backend discovered by the worker is grouped into AttentionGroup; the builder produces backend-specific AttentionMetadata from CommonAttentionMetadata.

core_modules.responsibility: torch.compile integration: FX graph splitting into piecewise submodules, Inductor pass pipeline, CUDA graph wrapping, and compile artifact caching.
core_modules.implementation_principle: @support_torch_compile injects TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper which calls torch.compile(backend=VllmBackend). VllmBackend splits the graph on splitting_ops, replaces compilable submodules with PiecewiseBackend (optionally wrapped by CUDAGraphWrapper), and per-range invokes CompilerInterface (InductorAdaptor/InductorStandaloneAdaptor/EagerAdaptor or an OOT compiler). PostGradPassManager runs fusion/no-op-elimination/IR passes inside Inductor.

core_modules.responsibility: Pydantic-dataclass configuration system. VllmConfig composes ModelConfig, CacheConfig, ParallelConfig, SchedulerConfig, CompilationConfig, SpeculativeConfig, LoadConfig, etc. and holds the current-config context manager.
core_modules.implementation_principle: The @config decorator (vllm/config/utils.py) wraps pydantic dataclasses with extra='forbid'. VllmConfig.__post_init__ resolves platform defaults, async scheduling, compilation mode, cudagraph mode/sizes, and optimization-level defaults. set_current_vllm_config/get_current_vllm_config implement a task-local global used by layers and compilation. compute_hash drives compile/model-info caches.

core_modules.responsibility: Distributed process groups and device communication: world/TP/PP/DP/EP/DCP/PCP groups, custom allreduce, NCCL/pynccl wrappers, all2all (DeepEP/MoRI/etc), KV/EC transfer connectors.
core_modules.implementation_principle: GroupCoordinator creates torch.distributed groups and an optional device communicator resolved from current_platform.get_device_communicator_cls(). initialize_model_parallel lays out groups in ExternalDP x DP x PP x PCP x TP order. Collectives can be routed through torch.ops.vllm.* custom ops for dynamo. DeviceCommunicatorBase is the OOT extension point.

core_modules.responsibility: Model registry, model loaders, weight loading/reloading, all model implementations, layers, quantization, fused MoE, rotary embeddings, and hardware-specific kernels.
core_modules.implementation_principle: ModelRegistry maps architecture names to (module, class) with lazy loading and subprocess-based model info inspection. BaseModelLoader creates the model and loads weights. Layers register themselves in a static forward context so the compilation system can bind KV caches and fuse ops. MoE and quantization are pluggable method classes.

core_modules.responsibility: Executor abstraction that fans out execute_model/sample_tokens/collective_rpc to workers. Implementations: UniProcExecutor, MultiprocExecutor, RayDistributedExecutor/RayExecutorV2, ExecutorWithExternalLauncher.
core_modules.implementation_principle: Executor.get_class() selects an implementation from parallel_config.distributed_executor_backend. All high-level operations are collective_rpc calls (non_block returns Futures for async scheduling). initialize_from_config allocates KV cache; determine_available_memory profiles the model.

core_modules.responsibility: Sampling (greedy/random/top-k/top-p/penalties/logits processors) and speculative decoding (Eagle/Eagle3/MTP/DFlash/ngram/draft model) with rejection sampling.
core_modules.implementation_principle: Sampler.forward applies logits processors then TopKTopPSampler. RejectionSampler wraps a Sampler, samples bonus tokens and invokes Triton rejection kernels. SpecDecodeBaseProposer/EagleProposer build draft inputs and call propose(). SpeculativeConfig constructs the draft model config.

core_modules.responsibility: User-facing APIs: offline LLM, OpenAI-compatible server (chat/completions/responses/models), pooling, speech-to-text, Anthropic/Cohere frontends, scale-out (token-in-token-out/render/derender), CLI, gRPC.
core_modules.implementation_principle: build_app assembles a FastAPI app; init_app_state creates the online renderer, OpenAIServingModels, and per-task serving objects. LLM wraps LLMEngine and adds preprocessing/beam-search/pooling mixins. api_server.py is now a deprecated shim over vllm/entrypoints/launchers/.

core_modules.responsibility: Plugin discovery via importlib entry points: platform, general, io_processor, stat_logger, endpoint groups.
core_modules.implementation_principle: load_plugins_by_group filters by envs.VLLM_PLUGINS allowlist and calls each entry point's load(). load_general_plugins runs all general plugin functions once, guarded by a module global. Platform plugins are loaded lazily during current_platform resolution.

implementation_principles.description: EngineCore.step() (core.py:633) is the heartbeat. (1) returns empty if scheduler.has_requests() is False. (2) calls scheduler.schedule(throttle_prefills) to get a SchedulerOutput (new/cached requests, per-req num_scheduled_tokens, spec tokens, encoder inputs, connector metadata). (3) submits model_executor.execute_model(scheduler_output, non_block=True) returning a Future (or list of Futures). (4) computes grammar bitmask via scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask(). (5) awaits future.result(); if the result is None (deferred sampling), calls model_executor.sample_tokens(grammar_output). (6) drains pending aborts. (7) scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_output) yields dict[client_index -> EngineCoreOutputs]. (8) attaches iteration details/stats and returns (outputs, model_executed bool). For max_concurrent_batches>1 (PP/async), step_with_batch_queue overlaps schedule and execute with a batch_queue to remove pipeline bubbles. EngineCoreProc.run_busy_loop repeatedly processes the input ZMQ queue then calls step_fn + post_step; InprocClient calls step_fn directly. Upstream/Downstream transport is msgpack over ZMQ; DPEngineCoreProc adds wave tracking, prefill throttling, elastic EP, and cross-engine barriers.

GPUModelRunner V1 execute_model (gpu_model_runner.py:4149): re-entrancy guard -> handle KV-transfer preemptions -> _update_states(scheduler_output) to sync the persistent InputBatch -> empty-schedule early return -> compute per-req num_scheduled_tokens -> _prepare_inputs(...) builds input_ids/positions/slot mappings/logits_indices (and spec metadata) -> _compute_cascade_attn_prefix_lens -> _determine_batch_execution_and_padding picks CUDAGraphMode + padding -> maybe ubatch slices -> KV update mode detection -> mamba align preprocessing -> _get_slot_mappings -> _build_attention_metadata -> _preprocess (MM encoder + embeds + positions) -> EPLB prepare_forward + padding mask -> forward inside set_forward_context(attn_metadata) calling _model_forward -> postprocess (PP send/broadcast, pooling branch via _pool, else slice logits and compute_logits). It then stores ExecuteModelState and returns None (or IntermediateTensors for non-last PP ranks). The executor then calls sample_tokens (gpu_model_runner.py:4530): unpack/clear state, apply grammar bitmask, _sample (Sampler or RejectionSampler), _update_states_after_model_execute, async PP broadcast of tokens, draft-token proposal (GPU-token drafters vs CPU drafters), _bookkeeping_sync, finalize KV connector, eplb_step, and build ModelRunnerOutput (or AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput). Overridable seams include _model_forward (explicitly documented), _prepare_inputs, _build_attention_metadata, _preprocess, _sample, _pool, _update_states, _get_slot_mappings, _determine_batch_execution_and_padding, propose_draft_token_ids.

vllm.platforms.__init__.resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname() first special-cases VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu, then loads OOT plugins from entry-point group 'vllm.platform_plugins' via vllm.plugins.load_plugins_by_group (which honors the VLLM_PLUGINS allowlist). It chains builtin platform plugins (tpu, cuda, rocm, xpu, cpu) then OOT plugins, calling each to test activation. Exactly one OOT plugin wins over builtins; >=2 of either raises RuntimeError; none => UnspecifiedPlatform. The module-level __getattr__ lazily instantiates the singleton current_platform from the chosen qualname so OOT packages can import vllm.platforms.Platform without recursion. OOT platforms subclass Platform and must override _enum=PlatformEnum.OOT, device_type/device_name, check_and_update_config (setting worker_cls), get_attn_backend_cls, get_device_communicator_cls, plus typically get_compile_backend/get_pass_manager_cls/get_static_graph_wrapper_cls and register_custom_kv_cache_specs. vllm-ascend registers NPUPlatform through this entry point.

AttentionBackend (backend.py:58) is an ABC whose static/class methods declare capabilities and validation. selector.get_attn_backend (selector.py:105) validates kv_cache_dtype, reads get_current_vllm_config(), decides whether block_size was user-specified, assembles AttentionSelectorConfig, applies per-KV-kind overrides from attention_config.backend_per_kind, then calls the functools.cache'd _cached_get_attn_backend. That delegates to current_platform.get_attn_backend_cls(selected_backend, attn_selector_config, num_heads). The platform-specific method (CUDA cuda.py:437, ROCm rocm.py:683, CPU cpu.py:138, XPU xpu.py:143) either validates the user-selected backend or iterates a priority list calling backend_class.validate_configuration(...) with ImportError/OSError guards, picks the lowest valid priority, and returns the class path. The worker later calls layer.get_attn_backend(), groups layers into AttentionGroup keyed by (backend, kv_spec, num_heads_q), negotiates kernel block sizes, and instantiates metadata builders.

A model decorated with @support_torch_compile (decorators.py:120) inherits TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper (wrapper.py:47), whose __init__ calls torch.compile(forward, fullgraph=True, dynamic=False, backend=compilation_config.init_backend(...)) -> a VllmBackend for VLLM_COMPILE mode. Dynamo traces and invokes VllmBackend.__call__ (backends.py:1015): it computes env/config/compiler/code hashes and cache dir, configures post-grad passes, splits the FX graph on splitting_ops into piecewise subgraphs, and PiecewiseCompileInterpreter replaces each compilable submodule with a PiecewiseBackend (optionally wrapped by the platform static-graph wrapper for PIECEWISE CUDA graphs). Each PiecewiseBackend compiles per shape range through CompilerManager.compile -> make_compiler (InductorAdaptor by default, InductorStandaloneAdaptor via VLLM_USE_STANDALONE_COMPILE, EagerAdaptor for eager, else OOT platform compiler). InductorAdaptor calls torch._inductor.compile_fx with monkey-patches (always-hit shape env, forced FX graph caching, hash capture). PostGradPassManager runs as the Inductor 'post_grad_custom_post_pass' applying fusion/no-op-elimination/IR-lowering passes. Results are cached and packaged into VllmSerializableFunction. CUDAGraphWrapper replays captured graphs keyed by (batch_descriptor, cudagraph_runtime_mode).

The scheduler creates a KVCacheManager (scheduler.py:308) from the KVCacheConfig produced during engine init. get_computed_blocks triggers prefix-cache lookup (coordinator -> per-group managers -> BlockPool hashes); allocate_slots allocates new blocks per group and returns KVCacheBlocks, flattening block IDs into SchedulerOutput (NewRequestData/CachedRequestData, num_common_prefix_blocks, new_block_ids_to_zero, kv_cache_block_copies, block_table_updates). On the worker, InputBatch.add_request calls block_table.add_row(block_ids); BlockTable maps manager block IDs to kernel block IDs (map_to_kernel_blocks) when kernel_block_size differs, computes slot mappings via a Triton kernel, and commits the GPU block table. build_attn_metadata constructs CommonAttentionMetadata(query_start_loc, seq_lens, block_table_tensor, slot_mapping, ...) per group, and each AttentionMetadataBuilder.build produces backend-specific metadata. AttentionImpl.forward reads block tables/slot mappings to index the paged KV tensors allocated by allocate_kv_cache and bound to layers by bind_kv_cache. Mamba/SSM caches and hybrid models go through MambaSpec and alignment logic in Platform.update_block_size_for_backend.

All hardware variance is funneled through current_platform (Platform subclass selected at import time) plus a handful of in-tree runner subclasses. Platforms override device capability/name/memory, dtype and quantization support (supports_fp8/is_fp8_fnuz/fp8_dtype/supports_mx), attention backend selection, compilation backend and pass manager, static graph wrapper, device communicator, KV cache layout and block size negotiation, custom kernel imports, pin-memory/inference-mode/sleep-mode support, and distributed PG initialization. Runner-level differences live in CPUModelRunner/XPUModelRunner/CPUWorker/XPUWorker and the MMEncoderModelRunner, while CUDA-specific concerns (custom allreduce, pynccl, cumem, NCCL) and ROCm-specific concerns (AITER, XGMI, AMDSMI, FNUZ FP8) stay in their modules. OOT platforms (ascend) inject a full Platform subclass plus Worker, AttentionBackend, DeviceCommunicatorBase, compiler, and KV specs through plugin entry points and patches.

module_dependencies.relationship: LLM/AsyncLLM/server create and drive the engine; serving layer calls EngineClient APIs.
EngineCore schedules via SchedulerInterface and dispatches via Executor to WorkerBase instances.
Scheduler allocates KV blocks, manages prefix cache, and produces grammar bitmasks.
Runner builds attention metadata against backends, binds KV tensors to layers, samples, and proposes draft tokens.
Backends are selected by the platform and consume KV specs, block sizes and CommonAttentionMetadata.
Compilation reads VllmConfig/CompilationConfig, asks the platform for backend/pass manager/static graph wrapper, and traces model forwards.
GroupCoordinator resolves the platform communicator; KV/EC connectors move cache between engines.
Models/layers register with the static forward context, use TP/PP groups, backends, and compile wrappers.
Platform plugins are discovered through the vllm.platform_plugins entry-point group during current_platform resolution.

hardware_abstraction_layer.ascend_relationship_summary: vllm-ascend is an out-of-tree package that activates NPUPlatform through the 'vllm.platform_plugins' entry point (single OOT platform wins over builtins). It must inherit/override: Platform, WorkerBase/Worker, GPUModelRunner (V1 and/or V2), AttentionBackend + AttentionMetadataBuilder + AttentionImpl, DeviceCommunicatorBase, CompilerInterface, AbstractStaticGraphWrapper, PostGradPassManager (or compose it), BaseModelLoader, KVCacheSpec/manager registrations, and KV/EC connectors. In addition, vllm-ascend applies monkey patches (patch/platform and patch/worker, documented in vllm-ascend's patch/__init__.py) to upstream classes such as the scheduler, model runner input handling, and linear/attention layers. The most sensitive upstream files are the ones listed under interface_surface and cross_project_relationship.definitely_affected_paths.

definitely_affected_paths: NPUPlatform directly subclasses Platform; any abstract-method/signature change (check_and_update_config, get_attn_backend_cls, get_compile_backend, get_device_communicator_cls, ...) breaks vllm-ascend at startup.
Platform registration/resolution logic determines whether NPUPlatform is selected; entry-point and name matching changes break platform boot.
AttentionBackend / AttentionMetadataBuilder / AttentionImplBase / MLAAttentionImpl are the base classes of every Ascend attention backend, builder and impl.
AttentionBackendEnum.get_path and register_backend are the mechanism Ascend uses to inject its attention classes.
WorkerBase is the base of NPUWorker/NPUWorker310/XliteWorker; constructor and deferred-sampling contracts are depended upon.
V2 GPUModelRunner is the base of the default NPUModelRunner (v2); execute_model/prepare_inputs/sample/initialize_kv_cache are overridden.
V1 GPUModelRunner is the base of NPUModelRunner (V1 fallback for LoRA/pooling/310P/spec).
InputBatch/InputBuffers are rebound module-globally to AscendInputBatch/AscendInputBuffers; field/layout changes break dummy runs and padded query_start_loc.
BlockTables.compute_slot_mappings contract and dtype (Ascend requires int32) are overridden by AscendBlockTables.
Ascend scheduler subclasses copy upstream schedule/update_from_output bodies; upstream refactors silently diverge.
Ascend KV cache specs subclass MLAAttentionSpec/SlidingWindowMLASpec/SlidingWindowSpec and rely on register_kv_cache_spec.
KV planning/prefix-cache behavior consumed by custom Ascend specs.
CompilerInterface is the base of AscendCompiler.
AbstractStaticGraphWrapper contract mirrored by ACLGraphWrapper (resolved via NPUPlatform.get_static_graph_wrapper_cls).
CUDAGraphMode/CUDAGraphOptions/BatchDescriptor and wrapper nesting contract are mirrored by ACLGraphWrapper/BreakableACLGraphWrapper.
VllmInductorPass base/context is used by Ascend fusion passes.
DeviceCommunicatorBase is the base of NPUCommunicator; collective API changes break TP/DP/EP and MoE communication.
GroupCoordinator is used directly; group construction and communicator negotiation affect Ascend device groups.
BaseModelLoader is the base of ModelNetLoaderElastic and RForkModelLoader; register_model_loader keys must stay stable.
MLAAttention/MLACommonMetadataBuilder are base/composition points for Ascend MLA support.
QuantizationConfig and specific configs are bases of the Ascend quant configs.
Protocol predicates (SupportsPP/LoRA/MoE/Eagle/HasInnerState) are implemented by Ascend-registered NPU models.
SpecDecodeBaseProposer/EagleProposer are bases of the Ascend V1 proposer family.
V2 speculator/CudaGraphManager contracts are bases of Ascend V2 spec decode (default MTP/Eagle/DSpark/DFlash path).
PunicaWrapperBase is the base of PunicaWrapperNPU.
ModelRegistry.register_model/get_supported_archs are used by Ascend's model plugin; the registry data itself is not modified.
potentially_affected_paths: vllm/config/**
Affects vllm-ascend only when the changed config field is read/written by NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config/apply_config_platform_defaults or by worker/model-runner initialization.
vllm/engine/arg_utils.py
Affects Ascend when CLI parsing, worker_cls/executor selection, or platform default resolution changes.
vllm/engine/core.py and vllm/v1/engine/**
Affects Ascend when engine scheduler/executor wiring or async scheduling contracts change.
vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py and metadata structs
Affects Ascend scheduler subclasses that consume/populate SchedulerOutput fields.
vllm/forward_context.py
Affects Ascend when additional forward-context attributes consumed by set_additional_forward_context change.
vllm/utils/torch_utils.py
Affects Ascend when device-agnostic helpers assume CUDA semantics; Ascend patches/replaces some of these.
vllm/triton_utils/**
Affects Ascend when Triton import/guard behavior changes; NPU Triton path may diverge.
vllm/distributed/** (outside device communicator)
Affects Ascend when distributed init groups or KV-transfer/EC-transfer base contracts change.
vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/** and mamba/**
Affects Ascend only for hybrid/Mamba models that use NPU model states (AscendMambaHybridModelState).
vllm/model_executor/models/** (individual models)
Affects Ascend only for architectures Ascend overrides or imports; generic model changes are usually transparent.
vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py (CommonAttentionMetadata re-export)
Partly used: CommonAttentionMetadata contract changes propagate to Ascend metadata builders.
vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py
Ascend uses ACL managers instead, but shared enums/helpers (CUDAGraphMode) may still be imported.
torch_npu and vllm.third_party/device ablation seams
Only when upstream changes generic device abstractions that torch_npu must satisfy.
never_affected_paths: vllm/platforms/cuda.py, rocm.py, xpu.py, cpu.py, tpu.py, openvino.py, neuron.py
Vendor-specific platform classes are never imported by NPUPlatform; only the shared Platform base matters.
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py, flashinfer.py, flashmla.py, mla/flashmla.py, mla/flashinfer_mla.py, mla/cutlass_mla.py, triton_attn.py, flex_attention.py, mamba2_attn.py, rocm_*
CUDA/ROCm attention kernels are never selected on NPU (Ascend selects its own enum overrides/registered backends).
Legacy v0 attention backends are not used by the V1 NPU path.
GPU-only quantization methods are not implemented on Ascend.
vLLM CUDA C++ kernels are never built or executed on Ascend.
Ascend uses ACL graph managers; CUDA-specific capture utilities are not consumed.
Ascend never edits the upstream registry; it only adds entries through ModelRegistry.register_model, so internal table changes alone do not break Ascend.

knowledge_base.patch_catalog_note: The analyzed repository is vllm-project/vllm. It contains no vllm/patch/__init__.py (the patch framework lives in the separate vllm-ascend repository under vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py). Therefore no upstream patch targets can be extracted. Baseline policy: any future commit touching the definitely_affected_paths must be evaluated against vllm-ascend's patch catalog separately.
